MANY SECTORS OF OUR ECONOMY ARE SHIFTING MUCH MORE RAPIDLY THAN ANTICIPATED TO BECOME MORE STEM-BASED. FOR EXAMPLE, SOME PROGNOSTICATORS SUGGEST THAT AS MANY OF 58,000 NEW HIGH-SKILL AGRICULTURE JOBS WILL DEVELOP BETWEEN 2015 AND 2020, WITH EVEN HIGHER RATES OF GROWTH POSSIBLE IN SUBSEQUENT YEARS. THIS RAPID GROWTH WILL REQUIRE A WORKFORCE WITH THE NECESSARY STEM SKILLS AND APTITUDES IF WE ARE TO CAPITALIZE ON THIS ECONOMIC POTENTIAL. IN ORDER TO SO, STUDENTS FROM RURAL AREAS WILL NEED TO PURSUE POST-SECONDARY STEM TRAINING AT HIGHER RATES. HOWEVER, IN OUR GEOGRAPHIC AREA SEVERAL BARRIERS PREVENT STUDENTS FROM OBTAINING POST-SECONDARY STEM DEGREES. WE SEEK TO REMEDY THIS THROUGH IMPLEMENTATION OF OUR PROGRAM, SUU PREP. WE WILL IDENTIFY SOUTHERN UTAH STUDENTS, ENTERING SEVENTH GRADE, WHO HAVE ALREADY EXPRESSED AN INTEREST IN AND APTITUDE FOR STEM FIELDS, BUT WHO COME FROM UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS, INCLUDING: GIRLS, CHILDREN OF COLOR, STUDENTS OF LOW SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS, STUDENTS FROM AN AGRICULTURAL HERITAGE, AND FIRST-GENERATION COLLEGE STUDENTS. SUU PREP WILL INVOLVE THESE STUDENTS IN A THREE-YEAR INTENSIVE ACADEMIC SUMMER PROGRAM INTEGRATING STEM DISCIPLINES WITH A FOCUS ON MATHEMATICS. SUU PREP WILL INCORPORATE BEST PRACTICES THAT HAVE BEEN DEMONSTRATED TO SUPPORT SUCCESS FOR UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENTS IN STEM PATHWAYS, AS WELL AS A TESTED CURRICULUM DEVELOPED OVER SEVERAL DECADES. OUR GOAL IS TO INCREASE THE NUMBER OF STUDENTS, FROM UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS, PURSUING POST-SECONDARY STEM EDUCATION. SHORT-TERM OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: IMPROVED ATTITUDE TOWARD STEM, INCREASED MATHEMATICS APTITUDE, INCREASED CRITICAL THINKING APTITUDE, AND INCREASED APTITUDE IN ALL SUU PREP COURSES.

WAMS-2-WAMS IS A SYNERGISTIC, MULTI-TIERED PROGRAM FOUNDED UPON EXPERIENTIAL STEM LEARNING, LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT, AND MENTORSHIP TO CULTIVATE A STRONG PATHWAY THAT MOVES WOMEN AND MINORITIES FROM RURAL HIGH SCHOOL CLASSROOMS TO CAREERS IN FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN (FANH) SCIENCES. RURAL WOMEN AND MINORITIES ARE UNDERREPRESENTED IN FANH STEM PROFESSIONS DUE TO LOWER RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION RATES. THIS PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THESE CAUSAL FACTORS AND CAPITALIZE UPON THE RESOURCES AND INFRASTRUCTURE WITHIN MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY AND ITS PROXIMITY TO RURAL K-12 SCHOOLS SERVING DIVERSE STUDENT POPULATIONS. WE PROPOSE TO ENGAGE AND EQUIP RURAL FEMALE AND MINORITY HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS IN AGRICULTURE-RELATED RESEARCH AND LEADERSHIP TRAINING UNDER THE GUIDANCE AND MENTORING OF SUCCESSFUL WOMEN AND MINORITY FACULTY WORKING IN FANH STEM DISCIPLINES. TECHNICAL KNOWLEDGE GAINED THROUGH PROBLEM-BASED, LEARNING EXPERIENCES WILL BE COUPLED WITH DEVELOPMENT OF PROFESSIONAL"SOFT" SKILLS (E.G., PROBLEM-SOLVING, TEAM WORK, AND COMMUNICATION). CAREER AWARENESS, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, AND LEADERSHIP SKILLS WILL BE ENHANCED THROUGH PARTICIPATION IN PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT TRAINING, NETWORKING OPPORTUNITIES, HANDS-ON RESEARCH EXPERIENCES, AND RESEARCH SYMPOSIA. AGRICULTURE IS THE TOP INDUSTRY IN THIS RURAL STATE. DEVELOPING THE PROFESSIONAL CAPACITY OF WOMEN AND MINORITIES IN AGRICULTURAL-RELATED STEM DISCIPLINES WILL PROMOTE SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE SYSTEMS AND RESILIENT RURAL COMMUNITIES AS WELL AS SUPPORT A WORKFORCE REPRESENTATIVE OF THE REGION'S CONSTITUENCY. THIS PROPOSAL ADDRESSES USDA STRATEGIC GOALS TO ASSIST RURAL COMMUNITIES (GOAL #1), CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES (GOAL #2), AND PROMOTE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION (GOAL #3) BY ADDRESSING THE EDUCATION NEED PROGRAM AREAS STUDENT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND STUDENT RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND EDUCATIONAL EQUITY.

MATERIALS HAVE ALWAYS BEEN LINKED TO HUMAN SOCIETY'S PROGRESS SUCH THAT PERIODS OF OUR HISTORY ARE NAMED AFTER THE DOMINANT MATERIAL OF THE TIME. THIS DEMAND FOR RAW MATERIALS HAS GROWN EXPLOSIVELY SINCE THE INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION. THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT OF MATERIAL CONSUMPTION IS PROPORTIONAL TO POPULATION, PER CAPITA CONSUMPTION (AFFLUENCE), AND TECHNOLOGY DEPLOYMENT. WESTERN SOCIETY'S TECHNO-ECONOMIC APPROACH TO DEVELOPMENT IS STRONGLY CORRELATED WITH ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION AND THAT AFFLUENCE IS NOT DISTRIBUTED EVENLY. IN CONTRAST, THE CONCEPT OF SUSTAINABILITY BALANCES THE COMPETING DEMANDS OF THE ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, AND ECONOMIC SECTORS. NC STATE UNIVERSITY'S DEPARTMENT OF FOREST BIOMATERIALS HAS SUCCESSFULLY INSTITUTED A STEM-BASED SUSTAINABLE MATERIALS AND TECHNOLOGY UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAM. PROGRAM FACULTY WANTS TO EXTEND THIS SUCCESS TO K-14 STUDENTS SO AS TO EDUCATE THE WORKFORCE OF THE FUTURE IN THE HOLISTIC DISCIPLINE OF SUSTAINABILITY. WE WILL START THIS EFFORT BY TARGETING STUDENTS WHO ARE AT THE COMMUNITY COLLEGE LEVEL. SPECIFICALLY, THE GRANT WILL FOCUS ON INDIVIDUALS WHO HAVE HISTORICALLY BEEN UNDER-REPRESENTED IN THE FOREST BIOMATERIALS FIELD: MINORITY WOMEN. THE PROJECT'S GOAL IS TO EXPAND OPPORTUNITIES FOR PROFESSIONAL CAREERS AND EDUCATIONAL EQUITY IN SUSTAINABLE MATERIALS SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING FOR THE TARGET AUDIENCE. THIS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED BY PROVIDING A MULTITIERED SUPPORT SYSTEM IN EVERY PHASE OF THE STUDENT'S POSTSECONDARY ACADEMIC CAREER, SPECIFICALLY THROUGH COMMUNITY SUPPORT, ACADEMIC MENTORSHIP, EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, COMMUNITY RESEARCH PROJECTS, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, AND UNIVERSITY SCHOLARSHIP/ADMISSION GUIDANCE. THE PROJECT WILL ENHANCE THE PARTICIPANTS' SCIENTIFIC AND PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES, LEADERSHIP AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS, PROFESSIONALISM, CRITICAL AND PROBLEM-SOLVING SKILLS, AND ABILITY TO WORK IN TEAMS. THE PROJECT IS BASED ON ACCOUNTABILITY; EACH PROJECT COMPONENT WILL HAVE ITS ASSOCIATED OUTCOMES ASSESSED USING PROVEN METHODOLOGIES. THE PROJECT'S GOAL AND OBJECTIVES ARE ALIGNED WITH NIFA'S STRATEGIC SUB-GOAL 1.7 (DEVELOPMENT OF HUMAN CAPITAL ... TO SUPPORT A SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE SYSTEM) AND ADDRESS WAMS' EDUCATION NEED AREAS OF STUDENT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND STUDENT RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND EDUCATIONAL EQUITY.

AS OF 2019, OUR ESTIMATED POPULATION IS 624,263 WITH OUR LARGEST CITY WITH 42,000. THUS, WE ARE A VERY RURAL STATE WITH SCHOOLS VERY SPREAD OUT.DESPITE THE RECENT DOWNTURN OF DAIRY FARMING IN THE STATE, AGRICULTURE IS STILL VERY CENTRAL TO THE WAY OF LIFE AND THE ECONOMY. IN FACT, THE NUMBER OF SMALLER DIVERSIFIED FARMS AND FOOD PRODUCTION COMPANIES IS GROWING. STILL, SIMILAR TO CHILDREN IN URBAN SETTINGS, VT CHILDREN, EVEN IN THE MOST RURAL PARTS OF OUR STATE, ARE DISCONNECTED FROM OUR LOCAL FOOD SYSTEM. ONE IN FOUR VT TEENS ARE OVERWEIGHT OR OBESE, WHICH LEADS TO SERIOUS HEALTH ISSUES LATER IN LIFE.FARM TO SCHOOL (FTS) ENRICHES THE CONNECTIONS COMMUNITIES HAVE WITH FRESH, HEALTHY FOOD AND LOCAL FOOD PRODUCERS BY CHANGING FOOD PURCHASING AND EDUCATION PRACTICES AT SCHOOLS. IT IS PLACE-BASED WORK THAT ENCOMPASSES A WIDE VARIETY OF ACTIVITIES, FROM CONNECTING CHILDREN WITH FARMS, TO SCHOOL GARDENS TO LOCAL FOOD PROCUREMENT, AND ENGAGES DIVERSE AUDIENCES RANGING FROM STUDENTS TO BUSINESSES ALONG THE SUPPLY CHAIN.VERMONT IS AN EARLY LEADER IN FTS AND HAS BEEN SUPPORTING SCHOOLS ACROSS THE STATE FOR NEARLY TWENTY YEARS TO ENGAGE IN ACTIVITIES RELATED TO AGRICULTURE, FOOD, HEALTH, AND NUTRITION.WHILE MANY VERMONT SCHOOLS ENGAGE IN SOME LEVEL OF FTS ACTIVITY, MOST SCHOOLS - PARTICULARLY IN RURAL AND ISOLATED PARTS OF THE STATE - STRUGGLE TO SUSTAIN AND EXPAND EFFORTS INTO STABLE, FULLY REALIZED FTS AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMS. SCHOOL DISTRICTS OVERSEEING EDUCATION IN RURAL REGIONS FACE MANY CHALLENGES: SCHOOLS ARE OFTEN SMALL AND GEOGRAPHY DISPERSED MAKING ECONOMIES OF SCALE DIFFICULT, STAFF RESOURCES ARE LIMITED, AND THERE IS A GENERAL LACK OF FUNDING FOR ONGOING TRAINING FOR KEY PERSONNEL.THIS TWO-YEAR PROJECT OFFERS A RURAL, DISTRICT-LEVEL APPROACH TO ENGAGING LOCAL AGRICULTURE, COMMUNITY RESOURCES, INTEGRATING LOCAL AND WHOLE FOODS INTO SCHOOL MEAL PROGRAMS, AND SCALING UP FTS IN UNDERSERVED DISTRICTS THAT FACE NUMEROUS CHALLENGES TO RECENT CONSOLIDATION OF INDEPENDENTLY OPERATED SCHOOLS. STATEWIDE PARTNERS SHELBURNE FARMS, NORTHEAST ORGANIC FARMING ASSOCIATION OF VERMONT (NOFA-VT), AND HUNGER FREE VERMONT (HFVT) WILL BUILD THE CAPACITY OF THE COMMUNITY PARTNERS (GREEN MOUNTAIN FARM TO SCHOOL, VITAL COMMUNITIES) TO SUCCESSFULLY DELIVER FTS PROGRAMMING DIRECTLY TO THE SCHOOL DISTRICTS' STAFF. THIS CONSTELLATION OF EXPERIENCED STATEWIDE AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS WILL PROVIDE WRAP-AROUND TRAINING AND TARGETED TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE IN TWO SCHOOL DISTRICTS TO DEVELOP BEST PRACTICES FOR CREATING SUSTAINED CHANGE. FOCUSING AT THE DISTRICT LEVEL, PARTNERS AND SCHOOLS WILL ADDRESS ALL ASPECTS OF WHAT IT TAKES TO BUILD SUCCESSFUL AND PROFESSIONAL SCHOOL MEAL PROGRAMS, AGRICULTURAL CONNECTIONS WITH EFFECTIVE FTS PROGRAMMING. THE PARTNERS WILL WORK WITH THE DISTRICTS TO FOSTER HIGHER LEVELS OF COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND ENGAGE CHILDREN IN EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING ABOUT AGRICULTURE, GARDENING, NUTRITION, COOKING, AND WHERE FOOD COMES FROM. IN OUR TWENTY YEARS OF SUPPORTING SCHOOLS WITH FTS, WE HAVE SEEN FIRST-HAND THE POWER THAT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING HAS ON TRANSFORMING STUDENT ENGAGEMENT, IN PARTICULAR WHEN THEY GET TO MEET DIRECTLY WITH FARMERS.THE LESSONS LEARNED THROUGH THE GRANT WILL BE SHARED NATIONALLY WITH PRACTITIONERS LOOKING TO SCALE UP FTS IN THEIR STATES.

THE GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO ENCOURAGE WOMEN AND MINORITY (WAM) HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS TO ENVISION THEMSELVES IN STEM FIELDS THAT RELATE TO FOOD, AGRICULTURE, OR FORESTRY BY ENROLLING THEM IN A PROJECT-BASED COURSE WHERE THEY CAN PERFORM ACTUAL RESEARCH, DISSEMINATE IT TO THEIR HOME HIGH SCHOOLS, AND DEVELOP KITS FOR BIOMASS EDUCATION TO BE FIELD TESTED IN K-12 SCHOOLS. THESE WAM HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS WOULD BE RECRUITED FROM RURAL NORTHERN LOUISIANA SCHOOL DISTRICTS TO ENROLL IN A PROJECT-BASED COLLEGE CLASS, "AGRICULTURAL WASTES TO PRODUCTS." THE CLASS WOULD BE OFFERED IN THE PI'S LAB FOR COLLEGE CREDIT BOTH AS A SPRING AND A SUMMER COURSE. THE COURSE WOULD ALLOW STUDENTS IN TEAMS TO RESEARCH CONVERTING AGRICULTURAL WASTES OR WASTE FORESTRY MATERIALS TO BIOPRODUCTS. LEADERSHIP OF THE TEAMS WOULD BE ROTATED TO PROVIDE EACH STUDENT WITH LEADERSHIP EXPERIENCE, WITH THE PI PROVIDING INDIVIDUAL MENTORING AND LEADERSHIP TRAINING TO EACH STUDENT. IN ADDITION, STUDENTS WOULD DESIGN KITS FOR USE IN EXPLAINING BIOMASS MICROSTRUCTURE, AND THE IMPORTANCE OF CONVERTING WASTE BIOMASS TO PRODUCTS, TO EITHER K-5, MIDDLE SCHOOL, OR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS. THESE KITS WOULD BE FIELD TESTED IN NORTHERN LOUISIANA SCHOOLS. SINCE LOUISIANA IS THE STATE WITH THE SECOND HIGHEST AFRICAN-AMERICAN MINORITY POPULATION AND IS ONE OF THE LOWEST RANKED STATES EDUCATIONALLY, THERE IS GREAT POTENTIAL FOR ADVANCING THE QUALITY OF EDUCATION IN LOUISIANA. THE PROJECT WOULD ADDRESS FOUR NEED AREAS: CURRICULUM DESIGN AND MATERIALS DEVELOPMENT; INSTRUCTION DELIVERY SYSTEMS; STUDENT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING; AND STUDENT RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND EDUCATIONAL EQUITY.

THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A FOOD SCIENCE PROGRAM CUSTOMIZED TO UNDERREPRESENTED SCHOOL GIRLS (8TH GRADE +) THAT WILL HELP INCREASE THEIR KNOWLEDGE AND INTEREST IN STEM-RELATED FIELDS WITHIN SUSTAINABLE FOOD SYSTEM. THIS HANDS-ON OUTREACH PROGRAM WILL ENCOMPASS FOUR (4) MODULES THAT WILL PROGRESSIVELY GUIDE THE ATTENDEES INTO CONCEPTS ON FOOD QUALITY AND FOOD MANUFACTURING AND THEIR USE TO IMPROVE FOOD SUSTAINABILITY, EXTEND SHELF-LIFE, AND REDUCE FOOD WASTE. TO EVALUATE AND MONITOR THE IMPACT OF THE FOOD SCIENCE CURRICULUM DEVELOPED, WE WILL PILOT THE INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIAL USING THE GIRLS INC. UMASS EUREKA! SUMMER PROGRAM. PROGRAM EVALUATIONS WILL INFORM CURRICULUM MODIFICATIONS, EXPANSIONS, AND REVISIONS. IN ADDITION TO THE ON-CAMPUS TRAINING PROGRAM AND TO OVERCOME THE GEOGRAPHICAL ISOLATION OF RURAL AREAS OR THE INABILITY OF RURAL POPULATIONS TO TRAVEL TO A LOCAL UNIVERSITY FOR STEM ACTIVITIES, THIS PROGRAM WILL ALSO DEVELOP A STEM KIT TO BE DELIVERED IN-FIELD AND OFFERED THROUGH LOCAL COMMUNITY PARTNERS (SUCH AS RURAL LIBRARIES AND 4-H ORGANIZATIONS). THE FOOD SCIENCE KIT WILL BE PORTABLE AND SELF-CONTAINED, I.E., IT WILL COMPRISE ALL THE REQUIRED REAGENTS, EQUIPMENT, AND SUPPORTING INFORMATION TO PERFORM THE ACTIVITIES. THIS KIT WILL BE SHARED IN RURAL COMMUNITIES BY MEANS OF LEARNING PROGRAMS DEPLOYED, FOR EXAMPLE, IN LOCAL LIBRARIES THROUGH NON-TRADITIONAL COLLECTIONS. THE AVAILABILITY OF THESE RESOURCES AT LIBRARIES LOCATED IN RURAL AREAS WILL ALLOW TO REACH A BROADER CONSTITUENCY AT IN-FIELD LOCATIONS AND PROVIDE THEM WITH NON-TRADITIONAL RESOURCES TO SPARK IN YOUNG GIRLS THE INTEREST IN STEM DISCIPLINES.

TEXAS TECH UNIVERSITY (TTU) PROPOSES A PROGRAM DESIGNED TO SERVE RURAL KINDERGARTEN THROUGH TWELFTH GRADE (K-12) TEACHERS AND STUDENTS. THIS PROGRAM IS DESIGNED TO ATTRACT AND INSPIRE UNDERREPRESENTED MINORITIES, DEFINED HERE AS FEMALE AND/OR FROM RACIAL/ETHNIC MINORITIES IN RURAL AREAS, TO PURSUE CAREERS IN THE AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES (AGRISCIENCES). VETTED AND PORTABLE LESSONS WITH ALL IMPLEMENTATION SUPPLIES CONTAINED IN TRAVELING LAB KITS (TLKS) WILL BE DEVELOPED FOR ELEMENTARY, MIDDLE SCHOOL, AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS THROUGH A COLLABORATIVE EFFORT OF TTU FACULTY AND K-12 TEACHERS, AND TRANSPORTED TO LOCAL, RURAL AREAS. PARTICIPATING TEACHERS WILL ACQUIREPROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND THE NECESSARY MATERIALS TO TEACH AGRISCIENCE CONTENT.THIS PROPOSAL ALIGNS WITH THE FIVE 2019 WAMS NEED AREAS. DIRECTLY ADDRESSED ARE: DEVELOPMENT OF CURRICULUM AND MATERIALS, FACULTY PREPARATION, AND IMPROVEMENT OF INSTRUCTIONAL DELIVERY SYSTEMS (THROUGH TLKS). THESE TLKS WILL ADDRESS THE 6 NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE'S GRAND CHALLENGES AND WILL BE LINKED TO THE TEXAS ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL ENABLE THE NATIONAL FARM TO SCHOOL NETWORK (NFSN) TO COLLABORATE WITH ESTABLISHED PARTNERS ON THE GROUND IN THREE SCHOOL COMMUNITIES: HARDIN SCHOOL DISTRICT 17H&1 IN CROW RESERVATION, MONTANA; INDIAN TOWNSHIP SCHOOL IN INDIAN TOWNSHIP, MAINE; AND MALAAI KULA IN KAUA'I, HAWAI'I. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL SCALE UP AND INSTITUTIONALIZE CULTURALLY SIGNIFICANT FARM TO SCHOOL PROGRAMS THROUGHOUT THE ENTIRE SCHOOL ENVIRONMENT AND ULTIMATELY IMPROVE THE NUTRITIONAL HEALTH AND WELLNESS OF NATIVE YOUTH. THIS PROJECT WILL BUILD UPON THE SUCCESS OF NFSN'S PREVIOUS WORK WITH NATIVE COMMUNITIES. WORKING WITH NATIVE PARTNERS, NFSN CONTINUES ADDRESSING THE UNIQUE OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES OF EXPANDING AND SUSTAINING FARM TO SCHOOL IN NATIVE COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY. FARM TO SCHOOL IS A NEW TERM FOR AN ANCIENT CONCEPT THAT EMBRACES INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE AND VALUES IN HARMONY WITH TRADITIONAL NATIVE LIFEWAYS, AND HAS PROVEN POSITIVE RESULTS ON HEALTH,EDUCATION, AND HUNGER. IN NATIVE COMMUNITIES, FARM TO SCHOOL IS ROOTED IN INDIGENOUS KNOWLEDGE TO TRANSFORM SCHOOL ENVIRONMENTS INTO CENTERS OF CULTURAL EDUCATION. THIS LEARNING TAKES PLACE IN OUTDOOR EDUCATIONAL SETTINGS SUCH AS SCHOOL GARDENS AND ORCHARDS, CULINARY PROGRAMS TEACHING TRADITIONAL FOODWAYS LIKE FORAGING AND PRESERVATION, AND SCHOOL CAFETERIAS SERVING INDIGENOUS FOODS TO EAGER STUDENTS WHO ARE RE-ESTABLISHING RELATIONSHIPS WITH TRADITIONAL FOODS. NFSN'S SEED CHANGE IN NATIVE COMMUNITIES PROGRAM WORKS AT THE LOCAL LEVEL TO EXPAND FARM TO SCHOOL ACTIVITIES (PROCUREMENT OF LOCAL AND TRADITIONAL FOODS, SCHOOL GARDENS, AND AGRICULTURE AND NUTRITION EDUCATION) FOR STUDENTS IN SCHOOL COMMUNITIES SERVING NATIVE AMERICAN YOUTH. NFSN'S SEED CHANGE PROGRAM MODEL IS BASED UPON HONORING LOCAL LEADERSHIP AND AUTONOMY THROUGH CAPACITY BUILDING TO SUPPORT THE COMMUNITY'S VISION AND TO ENSURE SUSTAINABLE PROGRESS. FARM TO SCHOOL ACTIVITIES ENRICH THE CONNECTION COMMUNITIES HAVE WITH HEALTHY FOOD AND LOCAL FOOD PRODUCERS BY ENHANCING FOOD PURCHASING AND EDUCATION PRACTICES AT SCHOOLS. OUR NEW RESOURCES WILL BE PILOTED WITH UP TO 400 YOUTH DURING THE PROJECT. OUR LONG-TERM AIM IS TO USE THIS NOVEL DISCIPLINARY SPACE TO SPARK STEM CAREER INTEREST OF MIDDLE SCHOOL-AGED YOUTH IN RURAL COMMUNITIES, WITH AN EMPHASIS ON GIRLS, TO BUILD NEW PIPELINES INTO CYBERBIOSECURITY CAREERS.

positiveFlows.title: NEW YORK IS THE 4TH LARGEST STATE IN THE UNITED STATES; COVERING 54,556 SQUARE MILES. IT IS COMPRISED OF 62 COUNTIES WITH POPULATIONS RANGING FROM LESS THAN 5,000 TO OVER 2.5 MILLION (1). NYS HAS A DIVERSE POPULATION: 12.3% ASIAN, 24.6% BLACK, 43.7% WHITE, 28.8% HISPANIC (4). POVERTY BY COUNTY RANGES FROM 4.8% - 29.7% (5); BUT EXTREMELY POOR COMMUNITIES HAVE RATES OF UP TO 48% IN KIRYAS JOEL (BRONX), 43% IN ITHACA (TOMPKINS COUNTY), 33% IN BINGHAMTON (BROOME COUNTY), AND 30% IN BUFFALO (ERIE COUNTY)(4). STATEWIDE, 21% OF CHILDREN UNDER THE AGE OF 18 LIVE IN POVERTY - 803,000 CHILDREN (5). IN ADDITION, 47.5% OF CHILDREN RECEIVE FREE OR REDUCED COST LUNCH; (74.9% OF CHILDREN IN NEW YORK CITY AND 31.7% OF CHILDREN IN THE REST OF THE STATE) (6). THIRTY FIVE PERCENT OF CHILDREN LIVE IN SINGLE PARENT HOUSEHOLDS. OVERWEIGHT AND OBESITY RATES FOR ADULTS (60.5%) AND CHILDREN (35.8%) ARE OF GRAVE CONCERN (7), AS THESE CONDITIONS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH SERIOUS CHRONIC HEALTH PROBLEMS, INCLUDING DIABETES, HYPERTENSION, AND HEART DISEASE. PEOPLE LIVING IN POVERTY ARE MORE LIKELY TO SUFFER FROM A VARIETY OF CHRONIC HEALTH PROBLEMS, BOTH PSYCHOLOGICAL AND PHYSICAL. WHILE ONLY ONE COMPONENT OF THE OVERWEIGHT AND OBESITY ISSUE, AND ONE OF A HOST OF CONCERNS FOR PEOPLE IN POVERTY, NUTRITION EDUCATION CAN MITIGATE BOTH. COVID-19 CONTINUED TO IMPACT PROGRAMMING ACROSS NEW YORK STATE IN FFY2022. MORE RURAL AREAS OF NEW YORK BEGAN TO RETURN TO IN-PERSON EDUCATION DURING THE SECOND QUARTER OF 2022, WHILE URBAN PROGRAMS HAVE CONTINUED TO REACH PARTICIPANTS VIRTUALLY. AS 2022 CONTINUES, PROGRAM STAFF ARE WORKING TO STRENGTHEN EXISTING PARTNERSHIPS AND BUILD NEW, AS MANY OF THE AGENCIES WHERE EDUCATION HAS BEEN OFFERED HAVE EXPERIENCED STAFF TURN-OVER AND/OR CHANGE IN OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES THAT HAVE IMPACTED THE SPEED OF A RETURN TO ‘NORMAL’ .  HISTORICALLY, IN NEW YORK, WE HAVE MAINTAINED A COMMITMENT TO A STATEWIDE EFNEP PROGRAM. WE HAVE DEVELOPED AND CONTINUE TO REFINE A COUNTY FUNDING FORMULA THAT INCLUDES ADJUSTMENTS FOR LEVELS OF POVERTY AND POPULATION DENSITY. HOWEVER, CONTINUATION OF LOCAL PROGRAM FUNDING IS CONTINGENT ON SUCCESSFUL ACHIEVEMENT OF PROGRAM OUTPUTS. ADDITIONALLY, COUNTY PROGRAMMING IS DETERMINED BY LOCAL BOARDS OF DIRECTORS. WE WORK IN CONCERT WITH COUNTIES THAT HAVE DETERMINED THAT NUTRITION EDUCATION FOR LOW-INCOME FAMILIES IS A PRIORITY PROGRAM AREA. GIVEN THE STATIC FEDERAL EFNEP ALLOCATION AND INCREASING COST OF PROGRAM OPERATIONS, THE NUMBER OF COUNTIES THAT CAN BE FUNDED HAS BEEN REDUCED SINCE THE LAST 5-YEAR PLAN. EFFORTS TO MAINTAIN AN EFNEP PRESENCE IN THE COUNTIES WITH THE HIGHEST NEED HAS BEEN A PRIORITY. AS A RESULT, 50% OF OUR PROGRAM FUNDS ADDRESS THE NEEDS AND POPULATION IN METROPOLITAN NYC AND LONG ISLAND.  COMMUNICATION WITH STATE LEVEL ORGANIZATIONS AND AGENCIES HAS REMAINED CONSISTENT AND ONGOING AND WILL CONTINUE TO EVOLVE. THE EFNEP COORDINATOR AND SNAP-ED STATE COORDINATOR SCHEDULE PERIODIC CALLS TO COORDINATE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, USE OF NUTRITION EDUCATION MATERIALS AND DISCUSS STRATEGIES FOR POLICY, SYSTEM, AND ENVIRONMENTAL WORK. ACROSS THE STATE, EFNEP REGIONAL COORDINATORS WILL CONTINUE TO NETWORK WITH BOTH PROGRAMS TO ENSURE QUALITY NUTRITION EDUCATION IS PROVIDED TO PROGRAM SPECIFIC AUDIENCES. CAMPUS LEADERSHIP WILL COLLABORATE WITH NYS SNAP LEADERSHIP TO PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND SUPPORT WITH POLICIES AND PROCEDURES, CONSULTATION ON INITIATIVES AND TRAINING AS NEEDED TO ENSURE QUALITY PROGRAMMING THROUGH LGU SNAP-ED PROGRAMS. SOME AGENCIES IMPLEMENTED STRICT COVID GUIDELINES, LIMITING ACCESS AND MAKING DIRECT CONTACT WITH PARTICIPANTS CHALLENGING. INCONSISTENCIES IN POST-COVID PROTOCOLS HAS HAMPERED BOTH RECRUITMENT AND LESSON DELIVERY.  THE TARGET AUDIENCE FOR EFNEP IN NYS IS LOW-INCOME FAMILIES WITH CHILDREN LIVING AT OR BELOW 185% OF THE FEDERAL POVERTY LEVEL; AND LOW INCOME, 4-H AGED YOUTH. COUNTY STRATEGIES ARE TAILORED TO ADDRESS THE SPECIFIC NEEDS WITHIN THEIR COMMUNITIES TO ENSURE SUCCESSFUL RECRUITMENT, ENROLLMENT, EDUCATION, AND GRADUATION OF PROGRAM ELIGIBLE INDIVIDUALS. COOPERATION WITH COMMUNITY PARTNERS, AGENCIES PROVIDING SERVICE TO THE TARGET POPULATIONS, AND COMMUNITY LEADERS WHO CAN PROVIDE INSIGHT AND GUIDANCE REGARDING LOCATIONS WHERE THE TARGET AUDIENCE LIVES AND WORKS, IS A PROVEN STRATEGY. STAFF ARE ENCOURAGED TO FORGE PERSONAL RELATIONSHIPS WITH KEY COMMUNITY LEADERS TO ENSURE THAT OUTREACH IS RELEVANT AND APPROPRIATE. GIVEN THE NATURE OF NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMMING TO LOW-INCOME AUDIENCES IN NYS, THERE IS LITTLE CONCERN FOR DUPLICATION OF SERVICES. STRATEGIES FOR IMPROVING SOCIAL MEDIA AND ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS ARE UNDER INVESTIGATION BY NATIONAL EFNEP WORKGROUPS IN WHICH NEW YORK STAFF ARE PARTICIPATING AND WILL BE PILOTED IN A VARIETY OF LOCATIONS DURING THE NEXT FIVE YEARS. WE ARE HOPEFUL THAT THESE TECHNOLOGIES CAN EXTEND THE REACH OF THE PROGRAM, BOLSTER ENROLLMENTS AND INCREASE GRADUATION NUMBERS. INVESTIGATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL POLICIES AND SUPPORTS WILL BE UNDERTAKEN TO INSTITUTIONALIZE COLLABORATIONS WITH PARTNER AGENCIES AND COOPERATIVE EXTENSION. PENN STATE EXTENSION’S EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP) PROVIDES FREE RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS TO IN COME-ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS TO DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS NECESSARY TO ACHIEVE A HEALTHFUL DIET ON A LIMITED BUDGET. OUR GOAL IS TO HELP THEM USE THE RESOURCES AVAILABLE IN THE MOST BENEFICIAL AND ECONOMICAL WAYS POSSIBLE.  THE PROGRAM CONSISTS OF A SERIES OF LESSONS, TAUGHT IN SMALL GROUPS, LED BY NUTRITION EDUCATION ADVISERS (NEAS) WHO ARE PART OF THE COUNTY EXTENSION STAFF. THE NEAS ARE PARAPROFESSIONAL STAFF HIRED BECAUSE OF THEIR COMMUNITY CONNECTIONS AND ABILITY TO BUILD RAPPORT WITH THE PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS. THEY ALSO SERVE AS ROLE MODELS FOR THE PARTICIPANTS. NEAS RECEIVE TRAINING ON NUTRITION EDUCATION AND ARE SUPERVISED BY EXTENSION EDUCATORS.  ALL EFNEP SERIES ARE FREE. PROGRAMMING IS HELD VIRTUALLY AND, WHENEVER POSSIBLE, IN- PERSON IN COMMUNITY CENTERS, LOW-INCOME HOUSING DEVELOPMENTS, LIBRARIES, CHURCHES, AND VARIOUS OTHER SITES. ALL SESSIONS HAVE HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES TO REINFORCE LESSON CONTENT, AND IN-PERSON PROGRAMMING INCLUDES FOOD DEMONSTRATIONS TO BUILD COOKING SKILLS AND ENCOURAGE PARTICIPANTS TO TRY NEW HEALTHY RECIPES. PENN STATE EXTENSION’S EFNEP DOES NOT SUPPLY FREE FOOD.  EFNEP PROGRAMMING TARGETS INCOME-ELIGIBLE YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS (18-25 YEARS OLD) WITHOUT CHILDREN, AND CARETAKERS OF YOUNG CHILDREN.  PENN STATE EXTENSION’S EFNEP ADULT PROGRAMMING COVERS FOOD PREPARATION, MEAL PLANNING, FOOD STORAGE AND SANITATION, SHOPPING SKILLS, FAMILY NUTRITION, AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY FOR A HEALTHY LIFESTYLE. THE YOUTH PROGRAMS INCLUDE FOOD PREPARATION, FOOD SAFETY, SNACK CHOICES, NUTRITION AND HEALTH, AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY. PARTICIPANTS MAY JOIN 4-H CLUBS OR GROUPS LED BY VOLUNTEERS AND PARTICIPATE IN REGULAR MEETINGS. THEY MAY ALSO HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO ATTEND SPECIAL SUMMER ACTIVITIES. YOUTH ACTIVITIES ARE ALSO AVAILABLE TO TEACHERS FOR IN-SCHOOL USE.  EFNEP EVALUATIONS CONTINUE TO SHOW PARTICIPANTS MAKING IMPROVEMENTS IN DIET QUALITY AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. EVERY YEAR, PENN STATE EXTENSION’S EFNEP HELPS 96-98% OF PARTICIPANTS MAKE A POSITIVE CHANGE IN ANY FOOD GROUP.

EFNEP PROJECT ABSTRACT  SINCE 1969, THE FEDERALLY FUNDED EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP) HAS BEEN TEACHING FAMILIES TO MAKE HEALTHIER FOOD CHOICES ON A LIMITED BUDGET, BE MORE ACTIVE, MANAGE THEIR FOOD RESOURCES, AND PREPARE AND HANDLE FOOD SAFELY. EFNEP HELPS LOW-INCOME FAMILIES AND CHILDREN GAIN THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS NEEDED TO CHANGE CURRENT ATTITUDES AND BEHAVIORS WHEN IT COMES TO CHOOSING NUTRITIOUS FOODS AND IMPROVING THEIR HEALTH.  DATA ON THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN HEALTH AND POVERTY INDICATE THE NEED FOR NUTRITION EDUCATION. THE NORTH CAROLINA JUSTICE CENTER REPORTED IN DECEMBER 2019 THAT OVER 1.4 MILLION NORTH CAROLINIANS (14%) AND ONE OUT OF EVERY FIVE CHILDREN (20%) ARE LIVING IN POVERTY. EAT SMART MOVE MORE NC REPORTS 68% OF ADULTS AND 31% OF YOUTH (10-17) ARE OVERWEIGHT OR OBESE. FURTHERMORE, TWO KEY BEHAVIORS, VEGETABLE CONSUMPTION AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY ARE ALARMINGLY POOR IN OUR CHILDREN. 41% OF YOUTH CONSUME VEGETABLES LESS THAN ONE TIME PER DAYAND 78% DO NOT MEET THE RECOMMENDED 60 MINUTES OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY PER DAY.  FAMILIES AND CHILDREN LIVING IN POVERTY SUFFER FROM HIGHER RATES OF OBESITY AND POOR NUTRITION LEADING TO OTHER HEALTH CONCERNS. RESEARCH SUGGESTS A STRONG CORRELATION BETWEEN POVERTY, FOOD INSECURITY, AND OBESITY AND A CORRELATION BETWEEN OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE.  NOT ONLY DO THE STATISTICS DEMONSTRATE THE NEED FOR NUTRITION EDUCATION, BUT 9 LISTENING SESSIONS HELD BY EFNEP ACROSS THE STATE IN 2019 ALSO INDICATE THE VALUE AND INTEREST IN NUTRITION EDUCATION OF STAKEHOLDERS. THESE LISTENING SESSIONS RESULTED IN THREE RECOMMENDATIONS: 1) PARTNER WITH HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS; 2) PARTNER WITH COMMUNITIES TO CHANGE THE NUTRITION ENVIRONMENT: AND 3) GROW AND EXPAND THE PROGRAM SO THAT HEALTHY EATING AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY BECOME THE NORM FOR CHILDREN IN NC.  EFNEP, DELIVERED THROUGH NC COOPERATIVE EXTENSION AND OPERATED THROUGH NC STATE UNIVERSITY, IS COMMITTED TO IMPROVING THE HEALTH OF LOW-INCOME FAMILIES AND YOUTH. EFNEP, THROUGH COOPERATIVE EXTENSION CENTERS THROUGHOUT THE STATE, EMPLOYS PEER EDUCATORS TO DELIVER A SERIES OF NUTRITION EDUCATION LESSONS USING EVIDENCE-BASED CURRICULA. PEER EDUCATORS PARTNER WITH LOCAL COMMUNITY AGENCIES AND ORGANIZATIONS TO RECRUIT AND ENROLL ELIGIBLE LOW-INCOME AUDIENCES. BY TEACHING PARTICIPANTS NEW KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS TO HELP THEM MAKE HEALTHY FOODS FOR THEIR FAMILIES WITHIN THEIR LIMITED INCOMES, EFNEP PROVIDES THE MOST VULNERABLE OF OUR CITIZENS WITH TOOLS TO ACHIEVE GOOD HEALTH ON A LIMITED BUDGET.

ABSTRACT: FY2023 EFNEP APPLICATION (THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA)  THE EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (UGA EFNEP) HELPS GEORGIA FAMILIES TO STRETCH THEIR FOOD DOLLARS, EAT BETTER FOR LESS, IMPROVE NUTRITION PRACTICES, AND PREVENT FOOD BORNE ILLNESS. FUNDED SINCE 1969 BY THE USDA NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE AND DELIVERED THROUGH THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION, EFNEP OFFERS PRACTICAL NUTRITION AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY INFORMATION, FOOD SAFETY EDUCATION, FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES, AND RECIPE DEMONSTRATIONS WITHIN COMMUNITY SETTINGS THROUGHOUT THE STATE. EFNEP INCLUDES PROGRAMMING TO A DIVERSE AUDIENCE OF ADULTS, YOUTH, AND CHILDREN WITH LIMITED-FINANCIAL RESOURCES. THE FOCUS SHOULD BE ON FAMILIES. SPECIFICALLY, EFNEP AUDIENCES INCLUDE LOW-INCOME PARENTS AND OTHER ADULT CAREGIVERS (SUCH AS GRANDPARENTS AND GUARDIANS) WHO HAVE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR OBTAINING AND PREPARING FOOD FOR THEIR CHILDREN, WITH EMPHASIS ON FAMILIES AND CAREGIVERS OF YOUNG CHILDREN AND LOW-INCOME PREGNANT WOMEN/TEENS. UGA EFNEP ALSO DELIVERS PROGRAMMING TO LOW-INCOME ADOLESCENT YOUTH (HIGH SCHOOL 9TH-12TH GRADE—AGES 14-19 YEARS). UGA EFNEP PEER EDUCATORS, WHO OFTEN LIVE IN THE COMMUNITIES THEY SERVE, DELIVER SERIES-BASED PROGRAMMING TO ELIGIBLE ADULTS AND YOUTH. THEY TEACH EVIDENCE-BASED NUTRITION CURRICULA DEPENDING ON THE AUDIENCE. (ADULT OR YOUTH) THAT INCLUDE INTERACTIVE LESSONS, RECIPE DEMONSTRATIONS AND EDUCATIONAL EXTENDERS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES FOR PARTICIPANTS INCLUDED: IMPROVEMENTS IN DIETARY QUALITY, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, FOOD SAFETY PRACTICES, FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND FOOD SECURITY, AS MEASURED BY VALIDATED FEDERAL SURVEYS PROVIDED PRE/POST PROGRAMMING (ADULT 30 QUESTION QUESTIONNAIRE, 9TH-12TH GRADE YOUTH NUTRITION SURVEY)

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY  TENNESSEES TWO LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS COMPRISE THE TENNESSEE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SYSTEM. THEY WORK INDEPENDENTLY AND COLLABORATIVELY TO CONDUCT RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ALL 95 COUNTIES AND TO SERVE THE STATES 6.9 MILLION PEOPLE. THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE IS BASED IN KNOXVILLE AND SERVES AS THE STATES 1862 INSTITUTION. IT INCLUDES THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE EXTENSION (UT EXTENSION) AND THE TENNESSEE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (UT AGRESEARCH). BASED IN NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY (TSU) IS THE STATES 1890 INSTITUTION; IT INCLUDES THE TSU COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM AND THE TSU INSTITUTE FOR FOOD, AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH. THIS PLAN OF WORK REPRESENTS THE COMBINED EFFORTS OF UT EXTENSION, UT AGRESEARCH, TSU COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM, AND THE TSU INSTITUTE FOR FOOD, AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH.  AGRICULTURE IS INTEGRAL TO TENNESSEES ECONOMY AND CULTURE. ALMOST ONE OF EVERY EIGHT TO NINE DOLLARS GENERATED IN THE STATE IS ASSOCIATED WITH AGRICULTURE OR AN INDUSTRY THAT GENERATES PRODUCTS FROM A NATURAL RESOURCE - MORE THAN $79.3 BILLION ANNUALLY. THE STATES AGRICULTURAL AND RELATED EXPORTS TOTALED $2.2 BILLION IN 2021, UP $325 MILLION OR 17% WHEN COMPARED TO 2020. TENNESSEE EXPERIENCED INCREASES IN ALL MAJOR COMMODITY CATEGORIES IN 2021. FARM RECEIPTS TOTALED $3.6 BILLION, WITH APPROXIMATELY 65.5% OF THIS VALUE COMING FROM CROPS AND 34.5% FROM ANIMALS AND ANIMAL PRODUCTS. IN ADDITION TO THE ECONOMIC SUCCESSES OF TENNESSEE AGRICULTURE, 339,400 TENNESSEANS ARE DIRECTLY EMPLOYED BY AGRICULTURAL OR NATURAL RESOURCE INDUSTRIES, MAKING EFFECTIVE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS CRITICAL. TENNESSEES LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS CONDUCT RESEARCH AND PROVIDE EXTENSION OUTREACH IN FIVE KEY AREAS TO ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES AFFECTING THE STATE: SUPPORTING FOOD, FIBER, AND ENERGY SYSTEMS; ENHANCING BIODIVERSITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY; ENRICHING OUR ECONOMY; DEVELOPING OUR WORKFORCE; ANDSTRENGTHENING OUR HEALTH. RESEARCH PROJECTS PROVIDE NEW KNOWLEDGE TO HELP STAKEHOLDERS ADDRESS ISSUES THAT AFFECT THEM. EXTENSION ACTIVITIES SHARE THAT KNOWLEDGE WITH STAKEHOLDERS ULTIMATELY TO RESULT IN A CHANGE IN ACTION OR CONDITION. MERIT AND SCIENTIFIC PEER REVIEW PROCESSES  TENNESSEE EXTENSION PROGRAMS FUNDED BY SMITH-LEVER OR NARETPA SECTION 1444 AND 1445 REQUIRE A MERIT REVIEW PROCESS. A PANEL OF EXTENSION ADMINISTRATORS, PROGRAM LEADERS AND SCHOLARS FROM FOUR STATES REVIEWED AND APPROVED THE TENNESSEE EXTENSION MERIT REVIEW CRITERIA. CRITERIA INCLUDES ASSESSING NEEDS, DELIVERY METHODS, IMPLEMENTATION STEPS, EVALUATION, ENSURING DIVERSITY AND DEFINED OUTCOMES. UT AND TSU COORDINATE MERIT REVIEW PROCESSES. STATE EXTENSION SPECIALISTS PROPOSE PLANNED PROGRAMS. ALL PROPOSED PROGRAMS ARE REVIEWED AND APPROVED BY A REVIEW TEAM OF UT EXTENSION ADMINISTRATORS AND SPECIALISTS.  UT AGRESEARCH WILL UTILIZE THE PROCESS THAT HAS BEEN IN PLACE SINCE IT HAS PROVEN TO BE BOTH EFFICIENT AND EFFECTIVE. HATCH REGULAR AND HATCH/MULTI-STATE RESEARCH PROJECTS UNDERGO A REVIEW PROCESS FOR MERIT AND SCIENTIFIC SOUNDNESS, AND TO ENSURE ALIGNMENT WITH ESTABLISHED RESEARCH PRIORITIES. THE REVIEW PROCESS FOR HATCH REGULAR RESEARCH PROJECTS BEGINS INFORMALLY WITH DISCUSSIONS BETWEEN THE PROJECT DIRECTOR, COLLEAGUES, THE DEPARTMENT HEAD, AND, IF APPLICABLE, AGRESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTER ADMINISTRATORS (IF FIELD WORK IS REQUIRED FOR THE PROJECT). A REVIEW PANEL OF THREE SCIENTISTS THEN EVALUATES THE PROPOSAL FOR CLARITY, TECHNICAL RELEVANCE, AND SCIENTIFIC MERIT. THE PROJECT DIRECTOR MAKES ANY NECESSARY REVISIONS AND SUBMITS THE PROPOSAL TO THE DEPARTMENT HEAD FOR REVIEW. IF APPROVED, THE DEAN/DIRECTOR OF AGRESEARCH THEN CONDUCTS A FINAL EVALUATION AND ENDORSES THE PROPOSAL FOR SUBMISSION TO NIFA.  HATCH/MULTI-STATE PROJECTS GO THROUGH A COMPARATIVELY MORE EXTENSIVE REVIEW AT THE REGIONAL LEVEL, SO THE INTERNAL REVIEW PROCESS IS ABBREVIATED. THE FACULTY MEMBER OFFICIALLY JOINS A MULTI- STATE PROJECT AFTER CONSULTING WITH COLLEAGUES AND, IF APPLICABLE, THE AGRESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTER ADMINISTRATORS. THE PROJECT DIRECTOR THEN SUBMITS A PROPOSAL REFLECTING THE UT COMPONENT DIRECTLY TO THE ASSOCIATE DEAN/ASSOCIATE DIRECTOR OF AGRESEARCH FOR REVIEW AND COMMENT. ONCE THE REVIEW IS COMPLETE AND ANY NECESSARY CHANGES ARE MADE, THE RESEARCHER SUBMITS THE PROJECT TO NIFA.  STAKEHOLDER INPUT  UT EXTENSION PURSUED MULTIPLE DATA COLLECTIONS FOR THIS PLAN OF WORK. OUR GOAL IS TO HELP THEM USE THE RESOURCES AVAILABLE IN THE MOST BENEFICIAL AND ECONOMICAL WAYS POSSIBLE. FURTHER USE OF REMOTE LESSONS AS SOCIAL DISTANCING GUIDELINES DECREASE IS DISCUSSED IN THE TECHNOLOGY PLAN. FLORIDA EFNEP WILL ALSO TARGET PREGNANT TEENS AND CHILDREN AND YOUTH IN GRADE K TO 12.

OHIO EFNEP 2024 PROGRAM PLAN SUMMARY ACCORDING TO THE 2020 CENSUS, OHIO'S POPULATION IS ESTIMATED AT 11,780,017. AS OF 2022 OF OVER 11 MILLION PEOPLE IN THE STATE 13.4% ARE LIVING IN POVERTY, COMPARED TO 11.6% IN THE U.S. OHIOANS' DIETARY BEHAVIORS ARE NOT OPTIMAL, IN 2022 , 36% OF ADULT OHIOANS REPORTED OBESITY WHICH IS HIGHER THAN THE NATIONAL AVERAGE OF 323%% (RWJF COMMUNITY HEALTH RANKINGS, 2023)). IN OHIO 10.7% ARE DIABETIC (11.3% NATIONALLY), AND 7.4% SUFFER FROM CORONARY HEART DISEASE (11.2% NATIONALLY). ONLY 12.2% OF ADULTS IN OHIO REPORTED CONSUMING FRUIT AT THE RECOMMENDED DAILY LEVEL; AND EVEN FEWER (9.3%) REPORTED CONSUMING VEGETABLES AT THE RECOMMENDED DAILY LEVEL. RESEARCH INDICATES THAT INADEQUATE CONSUMPTION OF FRUITS, VEGETABLES AND OTHER ESSENTIAL FOODS IS ASSOCIATED WITH OBESITY AND SEVERAL CHRONIC DISEASES INCLUDING CORONARY HEART DISEASE, STROKE, DIABETES, AND SOME CANCERS. INADEQUATE NUTRITION MAY ALSO BE ASSOCIATED WITH POOR BIRTH OUTCOMES SUCH AS INFANT MORTALITY. CURRENTLY THE INFANT MORTALITY RATE IN OHIO IS 7.0 PER 1,000 LIVE BIRTHS (5.79 NATIONALLY). AMONG THE 2,593,325 YOUTH IN OHIO, OBESITY IS ESPECIALLY PROBLEMATIC. DATA FROM 2021 YOUTH RISK BEHAVIOR SURVEILLANCE SURVEY (YRBSS) INDICATES THAT AMONG OHIO YOUTH, GRADES 9TH12TH:18.8 %. WERE CONSIDERED OBESE; 9.8% DID NOT EAT FRUIT OR DRINK 100% FRUIT JUICES, 7.4% DID NOT EAT VEGETABLES,17 % DRANK SODA, OR POP ONE OR MORE TIMES PER DAY AND 9.5% DRANK IT TWO OR MORE TIMES PER DAY; 24.6% DID NOT EAT BREAKFAST. REGARDING PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, THE YRBSS REPORTED THAT DURING THE 7 DAYS BEFORE THE SURVEY: 16% OF OHIO YOUTH (GRADES9-12) DID NOT PARTICIPATE IN AT LEAST 60 MINUTES OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY ON AT LEAST ONE DAY. THE EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP), FUNDED BY THE USDA'S NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE (NIFA), IS THE NATION'S FIRST NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM FOR LOW-INCOME POPULATIONS. EFNEP EDUCATION IS CONDUCTED THROUGH THE NATION'S LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS AND PROVIDES COMMUNITY-BASED, HANDS-ON EDUCATION. AUBURN UNIVERSITY EFNEP TEACHES LIMITED-RESOURCE YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND PREGNANT WOMEN AND TEENS THROUGH A SERIES OF LESSONS, PRIMARILY IN SMALL GROUPS, TO IMPROVE DIETARY PRACTICES AND BECOME MORE EFFECTIVE MANAGERS OF AVAILABLE RESOURCES. AU EFNEP HELPS LIMITED-RESOURCE AUDIENCES GAIN KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS TO IMPROVE NUTRITION, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND OVERALL HEALTH. EFNEP EDUCATION IS PROVIDED BY EDUCATORS WHO COME FROM THE COMMUNITIES THEY SERVE. THIS IS BASED ON THE EFNEP PEER-TO-PEER EDUCATION MODEL THAT EMPHASIZES BUILDING CAPACITY WITHIN LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES. THE FOCUS AREAS OF EFNEP ARE DIET QUALITY AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, FOOD SAFETY, FOOD SECURITY. THE TARGET AUDIENCE FOR AU ENFEP EDUCATION INCLUDES LIMITED RESOURCE ADULTS WITH CHILDREN, YOUTH IN GRADES 5-12, PREGNANT WOMEN AND TEENS. AU EFNEP REACHES THIS AUDIENCE THROUGH COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO SCHOOLS, HEALTHCARE, HOUSING SITES, COMMUNITY CENTERS, SOCIAL  SERVICE AGENCIES. DELIVERABLES/EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE: PROVIDE NUTRITION EDUCATION TO TARGET AUDIENCE; IMPROVE DIET QUALITY OF PARTICIPANTS; IMPROVE FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SKILLS; IMPROVE KNOWLEDGE OF PREPARING AND STORING FOOD SAFELY; INCREASE PHYSICAL ACTIVITY; PROMOTE PROPER INFANT NUTRITION; HELP MOMS-TO-BE HAVE FULL-TERM, NORMAL WEIGHT BABIES. SINCE 1969, THE EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP) HAS EDUCATED LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES AND YOUTH IN LOUISIANA, TEACHING THEM TO DEVELOP SKILLS TO MAKE HEALTHY CHANGES THAT WILL LEAD TO IMPROVED DIETS AND NUTRITIONAL WELL-BEING. THROUGH EFNEP'S HANDS-ON APPROACH, PARTICIPANTS LEARN TO MAKE BEHAVIORAL CHANGES AND IMPROVE THE NUTRITIONAL QUALITY OF MEALS FOR THEIR FAMILIES. EFNEP FOCUSES ON FOOD-RELATED PRACTICES TO HELP PARTICIPANTS ACHIEVE PERSONAL AND FAMILY WELLNESS. EFNEP DELIVERS RESEARCH-BASED TEACHING THROUGH A SERIES OF INTERACTIVE DIRECT-EDUCATION LESSONS TAUGHT BY PEER EDUCATORS WHO LIVE IN THE COMMUNITIES THEY SERVE. IN ADDITION TO DIRECT EDUCATION, LSU AGCENTER'S EFNEP PARTNERS WITH COMMUNITY AGENCIES TO IMPROVE FOOD AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY ENVIRONMENTS THROUGH POLICY, SYSTEMS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL (PSE) CHANGE INITIATIVES LEAD BY EFNEP SUPERVISING AGENTS. MOREOVER, THE PROGRAM IS DEDICATED TO REACHING DIVERSE, LIMITED-RESOURCE POPULATIONS IN NINE PARISHES THROUGHOUT THE STATE OF LOUISIANA. THE TARGET AUDIENCES FOR THE PROGRAM ARE URBAN OR RURAL LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES, PARENTS OR ADULT CAREGIVERS WITH YOUNG CHILDREN WHO ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PLANNING, PURCHASING AND PREPARING OF THE FAMILY'S FOOD; FAMILIES WHO ARE ELIGIBLE FOR USDA FOOD ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS; FAMILIES RECEIVING OR ARE ELIGIBLE FOR PUBLIC ASSISTANCE; LIMITED-RESOURCE PREGNANT TEENS AND WOMEN; EMERGING YOUNG ADULTS; YOUTH FROM FAMILIES PARTICIPATING IN AN USDA FOOD ASSISTANCE PROGRAM OR RECEIVING OTHER FEDERAL ASSISTANCE; YOUTH ATTENDING A TITLE 1 SCHOOL IN WHICH 51% OR MORE OF THE STUDENTS QUALIFY FOR FREE OR REDUCED-PRICE MEALS, AND YOUTH RECEIVING FREE OR REDUCED-PRICE SCHOOL MEALS. DURING THE 2023 PROGRAM YEAR, 5,987 RESIDENTS PARTICIPATED IN EFNEP EDUCATIONAL SERIES. SIX HUNDRED EIGHTY-FOUR ADULTS ENROLLED IN A NUTRITION EDUCATION SERIES DELIVERED IN HEAD START CENTERS, GROUP HOMES, COMMUNITY AGENCIES, ADULT LEARNING CENTERS, TECHNICAL SCHOOLS, PARENT GROUPS, HEALTH CARE CENTERS, PUBLIC LIBRARIES, TRANSITIONAL HOUSING FACILITIES, YWCA CENTERS, FAITH-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, PUBLIC SCHOOLS, AND OTHER GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS. ADDITIONALLY, 5,303 YOUTH ENROLLED IN A NUTRITION EDUCATION SERIES CONDUCTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH PUBLIC SCHOOLS, CAREER CENTERS, BOYS AND GIRLS CLUB, PUBLIC PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSIONS, FAITH-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, PUBLIC LIBRARIES, AND GRASSROOTS ORGANIZATIONS. A TOTAL OF 2,849 PROGRAM TOTAL FAMILIES WERE ENGAGED WITH EFNEP IN THE 2023 PROGRAM YEAR. EIGHTY-NINE PERCENT OF LSU AGCENTER'S ADULT PARTICIPANTS REPORTED INCOME AT OR BELOW 185% FEDERAL POVERTY LEVEL. PROGRAM OUTCOMES FOR 2023 IN THE CORE AREAS FOR ENROLLED EFNEP ADULTS INCLUDES 93% IMPROVEMENT IN ONE OR MORE DIET QUALITY INDICATORS, 86% IMPROVED PRACTICE IN AT LEAST ONE AREA OF FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, 67% IMPROVEMENT IN AT LEAST ONE AREA OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY BEHAVIORS, 73% OF PARTICIPANTS SHOWED IMPROVEMENT IN ONE OR MORE FOOD SAFETY PRACTICES, AND 31% OF PARTICIPANTS SHOWED IMPROVEMENT IN ONE OR MORE FOOD SECURITY INDICATORS. ENROLLED EFNEP YOUTH OUTCOMES INCLUDE 86% IMPROVED THEIR ABILITIES TO CHOOSE FOODS ACCORDING TO THE FEDERAL DIETARY RECOMMENDATIONS OR GAINED KNOWLEDGE, 56% OF YOUTH PARTICIPANTS SHOWED IMPROVEMENT IN SAFE FOOD HANDLING PRACTICES OR GAINED KNOWLEDGE, 59% IMPROVED THEIR PHYSICAL ACTIVITY PRACTICES OR GAINED KNOWLEDGE, 62% IMPROVED THEIR ABILITY TO PREPARE SIMPLE, NUTRITIOUS, AFFORDABLE FOOD OR GAINED KNOWLEDGE, AND 18% ACQUIRED SKILLS TO BE FOOD SECURE OR GAINED KNOWLEDGE. EFNEP ABSTRACT FOR RFA -- PENN STATE EXTENSION'S EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP) PROVIDES FREE RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS TO INCOME-ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS TO DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS NECESSARY TO ACHIEVE A HEALTHFUL DIET ON A LIMITED BUDGET. OUR GOAL IS TO HELP THEM USE THE RESOURCES AVAILABLE IN THE MOST BENEFICIAL AND ECONOMICAL WAYS POSSIBLE. THE PROGRAM CONSISTS OF A SERIES OF LESSONS TAUGHT IN SMALL GROUPS LED BY NUTRITION EDUCATION ADVISERS (NEAS) WHO ARE PART OF THE COUNTY EXTENSION STAFF. THE NEAS ARE PARAPROFESSIONAL STAFF HIRED BECAUSE OF THEIR COMMUNITY CONNECTIONS AND ABILITY TO BUILD RAPPORT WITH THE PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS. THEY ALSO SERVE AS ROLE MODELS FOR THE PARTICIPANTS. NEAS RECEIVE TRAINING IN NUTRITION EDUCATION AND ARE SUPERVISED BY EXTENSION EDUCATORS. ALL EFNEP SERIES ARE FREE. PROGRAMMING IS PRIMARILY HELD IN PERSON IN COMMUNITY CENTERS, LOW-INCOME HOUSING DEVELOPMENTS, LIBRARIES, CHURCHES, AND VARIOUS OTHER SITES. PROGRAMS ARE OFFERED VIRTUALLY, WHEN NEEDED, TO MEET THE NEEDS OF THE PARTICIPANTS. ALL SESSIONS HAVE HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES TO REINFORCE LESSON CONTENT, AND IN-PERSON PROGRAMMING INCLUDES FOOD DEMONSTRATIONS TO BUILD COOKING SKILLS AND ENCOURAGE PARTICIPANTS TO TRY NEW HEALTHY RECIPES. PENN STATE EXTENSION'S EFNEP DOES NOT SUPPLY FREE FOOD. EFNEP PROGRAMMING TARGETS INCOMEELIGIBLE YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS (18-25 YEARS OLD) WITHOUT CHILDREN, AND CARETAKERS OF YOUNG CHILDREN. PENN STATE EXTENSION'S EFNEP ADULT PROGRAMMING COVERS FOOD PREPARATION, MEAL PLANNING, FOOD STORAGE AND SANITATION, SHOPPING SKILLS, FAMILY NUTRITION, AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY FOR A HEALTHY LIFESTYLE. THE YOUTH PROGRAMS INCLUDE FOOD PREPARATION, FOOD SAFETY, SNACK CHOICES, NUTRITION AND HEALTH, AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY. PARTICIPANTS MAY JOIN 4-H CLUBS OR GROUPS LED BY VOLUNTEERS AND PARTICIPATE IN REGULAR MEETINGS. THEY MAY ALSO HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO ATTEND SPECIAL SUMMER ACTIVITIES. YOUTH ACTIVITIES ARE ALSO AVAILABLE TO TEACHERS FOR IN-SCHOOL USE. EFNEP EVALUATIONS CONTINUE TO SHOW PARTICIPANTS MAKING IMPROVEMENTS IN DIET QUALITY AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. EVERY YEAR, PENN STATE EXTENSION'S EFNEP HELPS 96-98% OF PARTICIPANTS MAKE A POSITIVE CHANGE IN ANY FOOD GROUP.

EFNEP ABSTRACT FOR RFA -- PENN STATE EXTENSION'S EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP) PROVIDES FREE RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS TO INCOME-ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS TO DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS NECESSARY TO ACHIEVE A HEALTHFUL DIET ON A LIMITED BUDGET. OUR GOAL IS TO HELP THEM USE THE RESOURCES AVAILABLE IN THE MOST BENEFICIAL AND ECONOMICAL WAYS POSSIBLE. THE PROGRAM CONSISTS OF A SERIES OF LESSONS TAUGHT IN SMALL GROUPS LED BY NUTRITION EDUCATION ADVISERS (NEAS) WHO ARE PART OF THE COUNTY EXTENSION STAFF. THE NEAS ARE PARAPROFESSIONAL STAFF HIRED BECAUSE OF THEIR COMMUNITY CONNECTIONS AND ABILITY TO BUILD RAPPORT WITH THE PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS. THEY ALSO SERVE AS ROLE MODELS FOR THE PARTICIPANTS. NEAS RECEIVE TRAINING IN NUTRITION EDUCATION AND ARE SUPERVISED BY EXTENSION EDUCATORS. ALL EFNEP SERIES ARE FREE. PROGRAMMING IS PRIMARILY HELD IN PERSON IN COMMUNITY CENTERS, LOW-INCOME HOUSING DEVELOPMENTS, LIBRARIES, CHURCHES, AND VARIOUS OTHER SITES. PROGRAMS ARE OFFERED VIRTUALLY, WHEN NEEDED, TO MEET THE NEEDS OF THE PARTICIPANTS. ALL SESSIONS HAVE HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES TO REINFORCE LESSON CONTENT, AND IN-PERSON PROGRAMMING INCLUDES FOOD DEMONSTRATIONS TO BUILD COOKING SKILLS AND ENCOURAGE PARTICIPANTS TO TRY NEW HEALTHY RECIPES. PENN STATE EXTENSION'S EFNEP DOES NOT SUPPLY FREE FOOD. EFNEP PROGRAMMING TARGETS INCOME ELIGIBLE YOUTH, YOUNG ADULTS (18-25 YEARS OLD) WITHOUT CHILDREN, AND CARETAKERS OF YOUNG CHILDREN. PENN STATE EXTENSION'S EFNEP ADULT PROGRAMMING COVERS FOOD PREPARATION, MEAL PLANNING, FOOD STORAGE AND SANITATION, SHOPPING SKILLS, FAMILY NUTRITION, AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY FOR A HEALTHY LIFESTYLE. THE YOUTH PROGRAMS INCLUDE FOOD PREPARATION, FOOD SAFETY, SNACK CHOICES, NUTRITION AND HEALTH, AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY. PARTICIPANTS MAY JOIN 4-H CLUBS OR GROUPS LED BY VOLUNTEERS AND PARTICIPATE IN REGULAR MEETINGS. THEY MAY ALSO HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO ATTEND SPECIAL SUMMER ACTIVITIES. YOUTH ACTIVITIES ARE ALSO AVAILABLE TO TEACHERS FOR IN-SCHOOL USE. EFNEP EVALUATIONS CONTINUE TO SHOW PARTICIPANTS MAKING IMPROVEMENTS IN DIET QUALITY AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. EVERY YEAR, PENN STATE EXTENSION'S EFNEP HELPS 96-98% OF PARTICIPANTS MAKE A POSITIVE CHANGE IN ANY FOOD GROUP.

SINCE 1969, THE FEDERALLY FUNDED EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP) HAS BEEN TEACHING ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS HOW TO MAKE HEALTHIER FOOD CHOICES ON A LIMITED BUDGET, INCREASE THEIR PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, MANAGE THEIR FOOD RESOURCES, AND PREPARE AND HANDLE FOOD SAFELY. EFNEP HELPS LOW-INCOME FAMILIES AND CHILDREN DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ATTITUDES, AND BEHAVIORS NECESSARY FOR MAINTAINING A HEALTHY DIET, THEREBY REDUCING THEIR RISK OF CHRONIC DISEASES. FUNDING WILL SUPPORT RESEARCH-BASED NUTRITION EDUCATION FOR ADULTS AND SCHOOL-AGED YOUTH THROUGH EVIDENCE-BASED CURRICULA IMPLEMENTED IN SCHOOLS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, HEALTHCARE SITES, AND OTHER PARTNER LOCATIONS ACROSS NORTH CAROLINA. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE TEACHING PARTICIPANTS HOW TO PLAN AND PREPARE HEALTHY MEALS, COOK FOOD SAFELY, ENGAGE IN PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND MANAGE THEIR FOOD BUDGETS. THE PROGRAM WILL ALSO OFFER TECHNOLOGY-SUPPORTED LEARNING THROUGH ONLINE LESSONS AND DIGITAL TOOLS, ALONG WITH COORDINATED RECRUITMENT AND OUTREACH EFFORTS WITH COUNTY PARTNERS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED DIET QUALITY, INCREASED PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, BETTER FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND ENHANCED FOOD SECURITY. PROGRAM IMPACTS ARE TRACKED THROUGH EFNEP'S WEB-BASED NUTRITION EDUCATION EVALUATION AND REPORTING SYSTEM (WEBNEERS). THE PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES ARE LOW-INCOME SCHOOL-AGED YOUTH AND FAMILIES WITH CHILDREN REFERRED TO THE PROGRAM BY COMMUNITY AND HEALTHCARE PARTNERS. THE COMMUNITIES THEY LIVE IN WILL ALSO BENEFIT AS PARTICIPANTS BECOME HEALTHIER, CONTRIBUTING TO A STRONGER PIPELINE OF HEALTHY STUDENTS, A MORE RESILIENT WORKFORCE, AND ENGAGED COMMUNITY MEMBERS, ULTIMATELY HELPING TO REDUCE HEALTHCARE COSTS.

PROMOTING WELL-BEING FOR MICHIGAN'S YOUTH AND FAMILIES REQUIRES ATTENDING TO INDIVIDUALS' PHYSICAL, SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH. TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH AND SAFETY OF MICHIGAN'S ADULTS, YOUTH, AND FAMILIES, WE DEVELOPED BROAD AND COMPREHENSIVE RESEARCH AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS TO ADDRESS MICHIGAN RESIDENTS' NEEDS. YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, NUTRITION AND FOOD SAFETY RESEARCH AND EDUCATION, AND FAMILY AND PARENTING SKILLS ARE IMPORTANT AREAS OF FOCUS. WE WILL SUPPORT MICHIGAN RESIDENTS IN EATING HEALTHIER, BEING BETTER CAREGIVERS, AND PREVENTING AND MANAGING CHRONIC HEALTH CONDITIONS THROUGH EDUCATION; DEVELOP BETTER MODELS FOR THE HUMAN HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES SECTORS; STUDY THE FUNCTION OF NUTRIENTS AND OTHER COMPONENTS RELATED TO HUMAN HEALTH; IMPROVE MANAGEMENT OF FINANCIAL RESOURCES BY INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES THROUGH EDUCATION; PREPARE YOUTH FOR LIFE AND WORK.

PROJECT ABSTRACT EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP) THE LOUISIANA STATE UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL CENTER'S EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP) CONDUCTS EVIDENCE-BASED, INTERACTIVE NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMS FOCUSING ON LIMITED RESOURCE PARENTS, CAREGIVERS, EMERGING YOUNG ADULTS, YOUTH, AND TEENS WITHIN COMMUNITY SETTINGS THROUGHOUT THE STATE OF LOUISIANA. EDUCATIONAL OUTREACH AIMS TO ASSIST PARTICIPANTS TO GAIN THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS NECESSARY TO IMPROVE BEHAVIORS THAT IMPACT FOOD AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, FOOD SAFETY, AND FOOD SECURITY. EFNEP CENTERS EDUCATIONAL EFFORTS THROUGH DIRECT EDUCATION DELIVERED BY PEER EDUCATORS. THE PROGRAM ALSO SEEKS TO IMPROVE ACCESS TO HEALTHIER LIFESTYLES THROUGH POLICY, SYSTEMS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL (PSE) CHANGES WITH COMMUNITY PARTNERS AND STAKEHOLDERS LEAD BY EFNEP PROFESSIONALS. THESE EFFORTS AIM TO IMPROVE ACCESS TO NUTRITIOUS FOODS AND ACCESS TO SAFE PLACES TO BE PHYSICALLY ACTIVE WITHIN MARGINALIZED COMMUNITIES. IN FY 2025, LOUISIANA STATE UNIVERSITY'S EFNEP SERVED 9 PARISHES THROUGHOUT THE STATE REACHING 1,348 ADULTS AND 8,258 YOUTH ENROLLED IN A NUTRITION EDUCATION SERIES.

VIRGINIA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION (VCE), A PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN VIRGINIA POLYTECHNIC INSTITUTE AND STATE UNIVERSITY (VT) AND VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY (VSU), THE VIRGINIA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (VAES) AND THE VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH STATION (VSUARS), ENABLES PEOPLE TO IMPROVE THEIR LIVES THROUGH RESEARCH AND EDUCATION USING SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE FOCUSED ON THE ISSUES AND NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS OF VIRGINIA. AUDIENCES ARE INVOLVED IN DESIGNING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EVALUATING NEEDSDRIVEN PROGRAMS. VCE, VAES AND VSUARS ARE DYNAMIC ORGANIZATIONS WHICH STIMULATE POSITIVE PERSONAL AND SOCIETAL CHANGE LEADING TO MORE PRODUCTIVE LIVES, FAMILIES, FARMS, AND FORESTS, AS WELL AS A BETTER ENVIRONMENT IN URBAN AND RURAL COMMUNITIES. VCE'S GOALS ARE TO: 1) DEVELOP AND TRANSFER NEW KNOWLEDGE IN APPLIED AND BASIC LIFE SCIENCES, 2) PERFORM RELEVANT, OBJECTIVE, AND TIMELY RESEARCH 3) IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR COMMUNITIES AND CITIZENS IN THE COMMONWEALTH, 4) USE A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO PROGRAMMING, WITH TASK-ORIENTED WORK TEAMS THAT RESPOND TO THE NEEDS OF INDIVIDUALS, GROUPS, AND ORGANIZATIONS, 5) WORK WITH AT-RISK, LOW INCOME AUDIENCES WHO NEED FOCUSED AND SPECIALIZED ATTENTION, 6) FULLY INTEGRATE A CULTURALLY DIVERSE PAID AND VOLUNTEER STAFF IN PLANNING, IMPLEMENTING, AND EVALUATING PROGRAMS, AND 7) RECRUIT AND COLLABORATE WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE PARTNERS TO BETTER UTILIZE RESOURCES, HEIGHTEN IMPACT, AND REACH A MORE DIVERSE AUDIENCE. WE WILL USE SCIENCE-BASED RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL STRATEGIES TO ADDRESS 1) CRITICAL AGRICULTURAL VIABILITY, P ROFITABILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY 2)OUR BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOMATERIALS, AND BIOENERGY PROGRAMS FOCUS ON ESTABLISHING REGIONAL COMMUNITY AND INDUSTRY NETWORKS TO IDENTIFY, RESEARCH AND EDUCATE ON UTILIZATION OF BACTERIA, WATER, PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND FORESTS PRODUCTS TO PRODUCE GOODS FOR HUMAN, INDUSTRIAL, AND AGRICULTURAL NEEDS FOR ALL VIRGINIANS 3) COMMUNITY VIABILITY PROGRAMMING WILL PROMOTE CONTINUING PROSPERITY AND FINANCIAL SECURITY FOR ALL VIRGINIANS 4) WE WILL ADDRESS FOOD SECURITY AND SAFETY, NUTRITION CHALLENGES AND HEALTH ISSUES FOR ALL VIRGINIANS; 5) WE WILL ADDRESS CRITICAL ISSUES OF NATURAL RESOURCE AND ENVIRONMENTAL ENHANCEMENT, PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION; 6) WE WILL SUPPORT STRONG, HEALTHY FAMILY DEVELOPMENT AND WELL-BEING LEADING TO STRONGER VIRGINIA COMMUNITIES; 7) 4-H PROGRAMS FOCUS ON DEVELOPING POSITIVE, HEALTHY, SKILLED, PRODUCTIVE YOUTH TO BE TOMORROW'S LEADERS.

MISSISSIPPI IS PREDOMINANTLY RURAL, WITH A POPULATION OF LESS THAN 3 MILLION, CONSISTING OF SMALL TOWNS WITH LOW POPULATION DENSITY, SLOW POPULATION GROWTH, AND HIGH POVERTY RATES. OVER HALF OF ITS COUNTIES ARE CLASSIFIED AS PERSISTENTLY POOR, AND APPROXIMATELY 12.8% OF HOUSEHOLDS RECEIVED SNAP BENEFITS IN 2024. MISSISSIPPI HAS LIMITED PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION AND HEALTHCARE ACCESS IN SOME LOCALITIES. THE GEOGRAPHIC ISOLATION, HIGH POVERTY, AND UNEMPLOYMENT IN THESE AREAS POSE BARRIERS, MAKING IT CHALLENGING FOR RESIDENTS TO OBTAIN FRESH, AFFORDABLE FOOD, LEADING TO HIGH LEVELS OF FOOD INSECURITY. FACTORS LISTED HERE MAKE MS A UNIQUE SETTING: 0.6% MS POPULATION DECLINE RATE OVER THE PAST 4 YEARS COMPARED TO AN AVERAGE GROWTH RATE OF 2.6% IN THE UNITED STATES (US), 54.4% OF RESIDENTS LIVING IN RURAL AREAS, 18% OF RESIDENTS LIVE IN POVERTY COMPARED TO 11.1% US, AND 27.9% OF CHILDREN LIVE IN POVERTY. MS HAS THE HIGHEST PERCENTAGE OF CHILDREN IN THEIR GRANDPARENTS' CARE IN THE US (7%), COMPARED TO 3% IN THE US. DIETARY INTAKE AND PHYSICAL INACTIVITY ARE TWO BEHAVIORS RELATED TO POOR HEALTH CONDITIONS. IN RECENT DATA, 4.1% OF ADULTS REPORTED CONSUMING 2 OR MORE FRUITS AND 3 OR MORE VEGETABLES DAILY, COMPARED TO 7.4% OF THE US. ADDITIONALLY, 13.4% OF MS STUDENTS DID NOT EAT FRUIT OR DRINK JUICES, AND 16.6% DID NOT EAT VEGETABLES OVER 7 DAYS. SIMILARLY, 33.4% OF MS ADULTS REPORTED NO PHYSICAL ACTIVITY OR EXERCISE OTHER THAN THEIR REGULAR JOB IN THE PAST 30 DAYS COMPARED TO THE US AVERAGE OF 24.2%, AND 24.8% OF YOUTH DID NOT DO 60 MINUTES OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY ON AT LEAST 1 DAY, COMPARED TO 15.8% NATIONALLY. MISSISSIPPI'S EFNEP FOCUSES ON SNAP-ELIGIBLE FAMILIES AND YOUTH. AN EMPHASIS IS PLACED ON PARENTS AND OTHER ADULT CAREGIVERS (I.E., GRANDPARENTS) WHO HAVE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR FEEDING YOUNG CHILDREN, PREGNANT TEENS, YOUTH, AND SCHOOL-AGED CHILDREN (KINDERGARTEN AND ABOVE), AS WELL AS PREGNANT WOMEN AND EMANCIPATED TEEN PARENTS OR TEENS WITH CHILDCARE RESPONSIBILITIES. WE WILL ENHANCE OUR EFFORTS TO REACH ADULT PARTICIPANTS IN COMMUNITIES WHERE THEY LIVE AND COLLABORATE WITH OTHER AGENCIES SERVING LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES. ADULTS WILL BE REACHED THROUGH HOUSING AUTHORITIES, CHURCHES, COUNTY HEALTH OFFICES, DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES OFFICES, FOOD PANTRIES, PARENT MEETINGS AT PUBLIC SCHOOLS OR HEAD START, COMMUNITY ACTION CENTERS, AND LIBRARIES. WE HAVE SUCCESSFULLY USED DIGITAL FLYERS POSTED ON SOCIAL MEDIA TO RECRUIT ADULT PARTICIPANTS. PARENTS ALSO RECEIVE INFORMATION INDIRECTLY FROM THEIR CHILDREN WHO PARTICIPATE IN EFNEP. YOUTH PARTICIPANTS WILL BE REACHED THROUGH PUBLIC SCHOOLS (99.7% OF MS STUDENTS QUALIFY FOR FREE AND/OR REDUCED LUNCH), BOYS AND GIRLS CLUBS, AFTERSCHOOL PROGRAMS, SUMMER PROGRAMS, LIMITED RESOURCE 4-H CLUBS AND SCOUT TROOPS, SUMMER FEEDING SITES, HOUSING AUTHORITIES, PARK AND RECREATION SETTINGS, AND CHURCHES. THE FOLLOWING COUNTIES (N=31) ARE PROPOSED FOR CONDUCTING EFNEP PROGRAMS IN FY2026: ATTALA, CHICKASAW, CLAY, COVINGTON, FORREST, GRENADA, HANCOCK, HARRISON, HINDS, JACKSON, JEFFERSON DAVIS, KEMPER, LAMAR, LAUDERDALE, LEAKE, LEE, LEFLORE, LOWNDES, MADISON, MONTGOMERY, NESHOBA, NEWTON, PEARL RIVER, QUITMAN, RANKIN, SCOTT, SIMPSON, SUNFLOWER, TALLAHATCHIE, WASHINGTON, AND WINSTON. TEACHING SKILLS THAT HELP LIMITED-RESOURCE YOUTH AND ADULTS EAT SMART, INCREASE PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND ACHIEVE A HEALTHY WEIGHT MAY CONTRIBUTE TO REVERSING MS TRENDS. FAMILIES LIVING IN POVERTY, ESPECIALLY THOSE WITH CHILDREN, ARE VULNERABLE TO FOOD INSECURITY, INADEQUATE NUTRITION, AND ILLNESS. EFNEP INFLUENCES BEHAVIORS THAT PROMOTE IMPROVED DIETS, FOOD CHOICES, FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, FOOD SAFETY, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND FOOD SECURITY, THUS MITIGATING THE IMPACTS OF POVERTY, FOOD INSECURITY, AND POOR NUTRITION. EFNEP CAN HELP IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF LIMITED-RESOURCE MS FAMILIES AND YOUTH BY PROVIDING NUTRITION EDUCATION THROUGH ITS VOLUNTEER, TECHNOLOGY, AND PARTNERSHIP POLICIES.

THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (KY EFNEP) PROVIDES RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATION AND RESOURCES TO IMPROVE NUTRITION AND FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AMONG LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES AND YOUTH. NUTRITION CHALLENGES MAY INCLUDE POOR DIETARY HABITS, LIMITED PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND UNSAFE FOOD HANDLING OR STORAGE PRACTICES. TO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF KENTUCKIANS EXPERIENCING LIMITED ACCESS TO NUTRITIOUS FOODS, KENTUCKY EFNEP IDENTIFIES COUNTIES AND COMMUNITIES WITH HIGHER RATES OF POVERTY. THE PROGRAM SERVES FAMILIES WITH YOUNG CHILDREN AND YOUTH WHO CAN BENEFIT FROM HANDS-ON, PRACTICAL NUTRITION EDUCATION. PROGRAM SPECIALISTS DESIGN AND DEVELOP CURRICULA, PUBLICATIONS, AND EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS THAT ARE APPROPRIATE AND ACCESSIBLE FOR THE INTENDED AUDIENCES. THESE MATERIALS UNDERGO A RIGOROUS PEER-REVIEW PROCESS AND PILOT TESTING BEFORE DISTRIBUTION. AUDIENCES ACROSS THE STATE ARE MULTIFACETED, AND EFNEP WORKS TO ENSURE THAT EDUCATIONAL CONTENT IS AVAILABLE IN FORMATS THAT ARE UNDERSTANDABLE AND USABLE FOR PARTICIPANTS. IN ADDITION TO OFFERING MATERIALS FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH LIMITED ENGLISH PROFICIENCY, EFNEP DEVELOPS RESOURCES TO ASSIST KENTUCKIANS WITH VARYING LITERACY LEVELS. EFNEP ALSO PROVIDES RESOURCES FOR PARTICIPANTS WITH DISABILITIES THROUGH BRAILLE TRANSLATION AND CURRICULUM ADAPTATIONS TO MEET PHYSICAL OR INTELLECTUAL NEEDS. ADULT CURRICULA ARE FURTHER ADAPTED BY SPECIALISTS TO ADDRESS SPECIFIC LIFE STAGES AND CIRCUMSTANCES, SUCH AS PREGNANCY OR PARTICIPATION IN RECOVERY PROGRAMS. YOUTH AUDIENCES ARE REACHED THROUGH SCHOOLS, SUMMER CAMPS, FAMILY RESOURCE AND YOUTH SERVICE CENTERS, AND OTHER COMMUNITY SITES OFFERING YOUTH PROGRAMS AND MEALS. UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF COUNTY-LEVEL FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES AGENTS AND AREA NUTRITION AGENTS, AND WITH THE SUPPORT OF STATE AND COUNTY EXTENSION RESOURCES, EFNEP PARAPROFESSIONALS COLLABORATE WITH COMMUNITY PARTNERS WHO PROVIDE REFERRALS, VOLUNTEERS, AND TEACHING LOCATIONS. PARAPROFESSIONALS USE GROUP EDUCATION METHODS TO DELIVER LESSONS AND RECRUIT PARTICIPANTS. THEIR STRONG COMMUNITY RELATIONSHIPS AND LOCAL KNOWLEDGE HELP EXTEND EFNEP'S REACH AND ENSURE PROGRAMS ARE RELEVANT AND ACCESSIBLE. KENTUCKY EFNEP MEASURES OUTCOMES SUCH AS INCREASED FRUIT AND VEGETABLE INTAKE, IMPROVED FOOD SAFETY PRACTICES, AND BETTER FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT. THE PROGRAM CONTINUES TO STRENGTHEN THESE OUTCOMES WHILE ENHANCING THE AVAILABILITY OF ITS EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES ACROSS THE COMMONWEALTH.

THE GOAL OF MISSOURI'S EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM (EFNEP) IS TO ASSIST MISSOURIANS WITH LIMITED RESOURCES IN ACHIEVING LIFELONG HEALTH AND FITNESS. OUR PRIMARY TARGET AUDIENCE IS ADULTS IN HOMES WITH CHILDREN. ALL PARTICIPANTS RECEIVE A MINIMUM OF SIX LESSONS. MISSOURI'S EFNEP PROGRAM WILL SHIFT ITS FOCUS IN FY2026 TO REACH ADULTS AND YOUTH THROUGHOUT RURAL MISSOURI. IN ADDITION, WE OFFER NUTRITION EDUCATION TO GROUPS OF YOUTH ACROSS THE STATE OF MISSOURI. THE OVERALL GOAL OF OUR PROGRAM IS THAT EFNEP PARTICIPANTS WILL IMPROVE OR MAINTAIN THEIR OVERALL HEALTH LONG TERM. BY SEPTEMBER 30, 2026, WE ANTICIPATE THAT EIGHTY PERCENT (92%) OF ADULT PROGRAM GRADUATES WILL IMPROVE ONE OR MORE DIET QUALITY BEHAVIORS AS DEMONSTRATED ON THE ADULT QUESTIONNAIRE/BEHAVIOR CHECKLIST. LONG TERM, OUR GOAL IS THAT ADULT EFNEP GRADUATES WILL BE MODERATELY PHYSICALLY ACTIVE FOR 30 MINUTES OR MORE MOST DAYS OF THE WEEK. BY SEPTEMBER 30, 2026, FIFTY-FIVE PERCENT (57%) OF ADULT EFNEP GRADUATES WILL REPORT THAT THEY PARTICIPATE IN 30 MINUTES OR MORE OF MODERATE PHYSICAL ACTIVITY MOST DAYS OF THE WEEK. LONG TERM, OUR GOAL IS THAT YOUTH EFNEP PARTICIPANTS WILL IMPROVE OR MAINTAIN THEIR OVERALL HEALTH LONG TERM. BY SEPTEMBER 30, 2026, WE ANTICIPATE THAT EIGHTY PERCENT (87%) OF YOUTH PROGRAM GRADUATES WILL IMPROVE ONE OR MORE DIET QUALITY BEHAVIORS AS DEMONSTRATED ON THE BEHAVIOR CHECKLIST. WE WILL ALSO EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF THE USE OF THE SNAC PROGRAM TO ENHANCE THE ENVIRONMENTS AND SYSTEMS IN WHICH YOUTH INTERACT LONG TERM, OUR GOAL IS TO KNOW THAT THERE IS A SAFE, ADEQUATE, HEALTHY FOOD SUPPLY AVAILABLE TO ALL COMMUNITY MEMBERS. BY SEPTEMBER 30, 2026, FOOD SECURITY OF EFNEP PARTICIPANTS WILL BE POSITIVELY IMPACTED THROUGH NUTRITION EDUCATION. NINETY-TWO PERCENT (92%) OF PARTICIPANTS REPORT DECREASING THEIR FOOD INSECURITY STATUS AS 92% OF PARTICIPANTS WILL REPORT THEY HAVE IMPROVED ONE OR MORE FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT BEHAVIORS.

THE EXPANDED FOOD AND NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM AIMED AT PROVIDING PRACTICAL HANDS-ON NUTRITION EDUCATION. EFNEP DELIVERS NUTRITION EDUCATION IN FOUR CORE AREAS: DIET QUALITY AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, FOOD SAFETY AND FOOD SECURITY. THE PURPOSE OF EFNEP IS TO ASSIST LIMITED-RESOURCE AUDIENCES ( ADULT AND YOUTH) IN ACQUIRING THE KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ATTITUDES AND CHANGE BEHAVIOR NECESSARY FOR NUTRITIONALLY SOUND DIETS AND TO CONTRIBUTE TO THEIR PERSONAL DEVELOPMENT AND THE IMPROVEMENT OF THE TOTAL FAMILY DIET AND NUTRITIONAL WELLBEING. OVERALL EFNEP OUTCOMES INCLUDES INCREASED KNOWLEDGE OF THE ESSENTIALS OF HUMAN NUTRITION, INCREASED ABILITY TO SELECT AND BUY FOOD THAT SATISFY NUTRITIONAL NEEDS, IMPROVED PRACTICES IN FOOD PRODUCTION, PREPARATION, STORAGE, SAFETY AND SANITATION, IMPROVED ABILITY TO MANAGE FOOD BUDGETS AND FOOD RESOURCES AND INCREASED RATE OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY.

EFNEP PUERTO RICO IS A LEADING INITIATIVE DEDICATED TO IMPROVING THE NUTRITIONAL HEALTH OF LOW-INCOME FAMILIES THROUGH EDUCATION AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT. THE PROGRAM FOCUSES ON FOUR KEY AREAS: ENHANCING DIET QUALITY AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY BY PROMOTING FEDERAL GUIDELINES FOR HEALTHY LIVING; STRENGTHENING FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT SKILLS TO HELP FAMILIES BUY, PREPARE, AND STORE NUTRITIOUS FOOD; IMPROVING HOUSEHOLD FOOD SAFETY AND SANITATION PRACTICES; AND INCREASING FOOD SECURITY BY CONNECTING PARTICIPANTS WITH LOCAL FARMERS, PRODUCERS, AND FOOD ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS. NUTRITION EDUCATION IS DELIVERED BY PARAPROFESSIONALS ACROSS FIVE REGIONAL UNITS-ARECIBO, CAGUAS, COAMO, SAN JUAN, AND TOA BAJA-TARGETING LOW-INCOME ADULTS WITH CHILDREN AND YOUTH, ESPECIALLY THOSE RESPONSIBLE FOR FOOD PLANNING AND PREPARATION. THESE EFFORTS ARE SUPPORTED BY VOLUNTEERS, AGENCIES, AND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS. CHILDREN AND YOUTH FROM THIRD TO TWELFTH GRADE ARE ALSO SERVED THROUGH SCHOOLS, HOMESCHOOLING GROUPS, SUMMER CAMPS, AND OTHER COMMUNITY SETTINGS, WITH A PILOT POLICY, SYSTEM, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE (PSE) PROGRAM INTRODUCED FOR K-3RD GRADE STUDENTS. CURRICULA INCLUDE THE SPANISH VERSION OF EATING SMART - BEING ACTIVE FOR ADULTS, DEVELOPED BY COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY, WHICH COVERS FOOD GROUPS, PREPARATION, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, FOOD SAFETY, AND HEALTHY CHOICES; LIVE HEALTHY AND ACTIVE (VIVE SALUDABLE Y ACTIVO) FOR CHILDREN IN GRADES 3-5; AND NUTRITION CHALLENGE FOR YOUTH IN GRADES 9-12, BOTH OFFERING SIX LESSONS ON HEALTHIER LIFESTYLE CHOICES. THROUGH HANDS-ON LEARNING, RECIPE DEMONSTRATIONS, AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, EFNEP EMPOWERS FAMILIES TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS, IMPROVE THEIR ABILITY TO SECURE NUTRITIOUS FOOD, AND BUILD HEALTHIER LIVES. BEYOND IMPROVING HEALTH OUTCOMES, EFNEP ALSO CONTRIBUTES TO PUERTO RICO'S ECONOMIC VITALITY BY HELPING FAMILIES STRETCH THEIR FOOD DOLLARS, REDUCE WASTE, MAKE COST-EFFECTIVE CHOICES THAT STRENGTHEN HOUSEHOLD FINANCES AND REDUCES DEPENDENCY, AS WELL AS STRENGTHEN LOCAL FOOD SYSTEMS AND AMERICAN FARMERS WELLBEING. WITH THE LAUNCH OF THIS PROGRAM, WE ARE INTENSIFYING EFFORTS TO RECRUIT PARTICIPANTS INTO COMMUNITY UNITS THAT FOSTER EDUCATION, SUPPORT, AND HOLISTIC WELL-BEING, CREATING STRONGER, MORE RESILIENT COMMUNITIES WHERE WELLNESS BEGINS IN THE KITCHEN AND FLOURISHES IN EVERYDAY LIFE.

THE PURPOSE OF EFNEP IS TO PROVIDE NUTRITION EDUCATION TO LOW- INCOME POPULATIONS TO REDUCE NUTRITION INSECURITY IN LOW INCOME FAMILIES AND YOUTH. EFNEP OBJECTIVES INCLUDE PROVIDING ASSISTANCE TO LOW-INCOME FAMILIES AND YOUTH IN ACQUIRING KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ATTITUDES AND CHANGED BEHAVIORS NECESSARY FOR NUTRITIONALLY SOUND DIETS, AND TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE OVERALL IMPROVEMENT OF THE TOTAL FAMILY DIET AND NUTRITIONAL WELL-BEING. THIS IS ACCOMPLISHED BY PROVIDING INFORMAL AND EASILY ACCESSIBLE NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMS IN THE COMMUNITY. PEER EDUCATORS, WHO TYPICALLY LIVE IN THE COMMUNITIES THEY WORK, DELIVER A SERIES OF INTERACTIVE LESSONS TO PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS IN COMMUNITY SETTINGS. THE LESSONS ARE EVIDENCE-BASED AND ARE TAILORED TO MEET THE NEEDS OF THE AUDIENCE. THE PROGRAM LESSONS FOCUS ON DEVELOPING KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS RELATED TO NUTRITION, DIET QUALITY, MEAL PREPARATION AND SAFETY, RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY.
